subject: Sunridge: sustained completion tail & concurrency cap mitigation
messages:
From: Dana Leary <dana.leary@sunridge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurements@sunridge.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Sunridge: increased p99/p999 completions (urgent)

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sustained spike in p99 and p999 completion latency across our production traffic starting ~08:45 PDT. Brief symptoms: timeouts on our webhook consumer, multiple orders failing to finish within our 10s client timeout, and intermittent 502s from the Redwood endpoint. Our SREs pulled a few traces and we have several requests with completion times > 12s and a couple hitting 20s+.

This is affecting checkout flows for a subset of our enterprise customers (approx 12% of requests). Can you confirm whether this is a platform-side issue or something on our integration? We flagged this as P0 because our transactional success rate dropped ~6% for the last 45m.

- Dana

Subject: Re: Sunridge: increased p99/p999 completions (urgent)

Karthik / Marissa —

Triage summary (quick):
- Observed behavior: p50/p95 within expected envelope. p99 and p999 show multi-second spikes starting 08:40. Our per-tenant concurrency controller logged sustained 'cap_reached' events for tenant sunridge-acct (policy: per-tenant concurrency cap = 10).
- Root cause hypothesis: a small fraction of long-running requests (large-context, ~8k tokens) are occupying inference workers and causing head-of-line blocking. Because we enforce a strict per-tenant concurrency cap, incoming burst requests are queued at the front-end (request router) and then scheduled -> this creates longer queue residency for subsequent short requests (checkout) leading to tail amplification.
- Telemetry / evidence: sample traces IDs: trc-7f9b, trc-7fb0. KV cache warmup times for these traces are ~150ms extra per request (since warm cache misses hit on many of the long prompts), and we see increased scheduling retries in the worker logs.

Immediate mitigations (recommendations):
1) Temporary bump per-tenant concurrency cap from 10 -> 20 for sunridge-acct for 72 hours (can be revoked). This reduces queueing and spreads load across more workers. Risk: cost increase and potential noisy neighbor effects if not paired with routing to larger pool.
2) Enable quick-fail path for short timeouts: route requests with <=512 tokens to a low-latency optimized shard (model variant: m-optim-lt) to keep checkout flows responsive.
3) Prime KV cache for the 15 most common prefixes observed in sample traces (script attached). That reduces warmup penalty.
4) Canary roll: perform a canary bump for 10% of traffic first, validate p999 drop, then roll to 100% in 30m if green.

Attachments: 20270901-sunridge-traces.csv (raw traces), runbook snippet: bump_concurrency.md

I'll start the canary and prepare a short rollback plan. If we get green on canary, we should keep the cap increase for 48–72 hours while we monitor for neighbor impact.

- Dev Patel
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick triage. We primarily see the long-context checkout flows causing the issues (customer prompts with appended cart history). The routing to an LT-optimized shard sounds promising. If you need us to toggle any client-side flags (e.g., split requests or reduce max tokens), we can try, but this will require a release and coordination.

Two asks from our side:
1) Timeline for the canary and full mitigation (we need ETA to communicate to customers).
2) Given the impact to revenue-critical checkouts, Sunridge will want to discuss SLA credit / one-off mitigation budget if this persists beyond 24 hours. Please let us know how Redwood is thinking about credits for incidents with platform-side queuing causes.

We can join the 10:00 sync.

- Dana
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Sunridge post-mitigation exec note and escalation (for approval)

Team —

Post-mort summary and ask:
- Incident window: 2027-09-01 08:40–10:05 PDT. Customer impact: ~12% of Sunridge requests saw degraded success for ~85 minutes; p999 reduced from 18s -> 3.6s after mitigation.
- Root cause: per-tenant concurrency cap (10) + a small set of long-context requests creating head-of-line blocking and KV cache warmups.
- Actions taken: canary bump of concurrency cap to 20 for 10% traffic at 09:05 PDT, validated improvement; broad bump to 100% at 09:20 with routing of <=512-token requests to m-optim-lt pool; KV priming completed by 09:40.
- Outcome: p999 reduced to acceptable levels, webhook timeouts cleared, and no neighbor-tenant SLA anomalies detected in the 24h window. Cost impact: estimated incremental spend for 72h bump = $3.9k.

Executive asks:
1) Approve a one-week dedicated burst (reserved pool) for Sunridge while they finalize client-side prompt reductions. Estimated cost (discounted) presented: $8k/week. This gives capacity headroom and prevents recurrence.
2) Approve a one-time credit to Sunridge of 20% of last month’s bill as a goodwill gesture (revenue ops has signoff threshold at $10k). We estimate the credit impact ~ $6.2k.

We have a customer sync scheduled Monday 09/06 to confirm the longer-term plan (prompt changes + reservation). Please reply with approvals or escalate any objections.

- Karthik
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
